questions.prompt: For centred data with covariance C, which unit vector v maximizes the variance v^T C v of the projected data?
options: The eigenvector of C with the largest eigenvalue
Any vector, since projection preserves variance
The eigenvector of C with the smallest eigenvalue
The direction of the largest single data point
questions.explanation: v^T C v = Σ λ_j a_j² ≤ λ_max, with equality for the top eigenvector.

questions.prompt: Centred covariance C = [[2.5, 1.5],[1.5, 2.5]]. What fraction of total variance does the first principal component explain? (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
Centred covariance C = [[2.5, 1.5],[1.5, 2.5]]. What is the mean squared reconstruction error when keeping only the first principal component? (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
questions.explanation: The error equals the dropped eigenvalue λ₂=1.

questions.prompt: Compute the cosine similarity of u=(1,2,2) and v=(2,1,2). (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
An embedding table has a vocabulary of 20,000 items and 128 dimensions. How many parameters does it have? (integer, tolerance 1)
A frozen PCA encoder is evaluated by training a classifier head on 10 labelled points and testing on held-out points. Which result best supports 'the features are good'?
options: Higher training accuracy than on raw inputs, measured on one particular labelled set of 10 points
Higher mean held-out accuracy than the same head on raw inputs, over many labelled-set draws
The encoder has fewer output dimensions than input dimensions, so it compresses the data usefully
A low reconstruction error on the training pool, since the code then keeps the information
questions.explanation: Quality is a held-out, task-level claim compared with a baseline; training accuracy and reconstruction error do not establish it.

questions.prompt: PCA features computed from unlabelled sensor data give chance-level accuracy for your classifier. Give two possible explanations and the check you would run for each.
rubric: Variance is dominated by a nuisance factor, so the label-relevant direction was dropped; check by using more components or class-conditional variance.
The encoder was fitted on a different distribution, or the pipeline has a bug (not centred, wrong projection); check on the worked toy case and invariants.
Compares with the raw-input baseline over several label draws and states what result would reject each explanation.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
